rule: True FF is a separate renderer. A commit that changes the normalized source of any protected non-FF render file must carry 'Non-FF-Render-Change: <reason>'; normalization ignores comments and whitespace only (string literals, #define and #include lines count). A config change that removes protection from a tracked file counts as a change to that file. No protected shader (.glsl/.glslinc/.gdshader/.gdshaderinc) may include an FF-private file. Merge commits are checked against the first parent (HEAD), the line the merge lands on. Fail closed: with no HEAD, or no config at HEAD, every staged protected file counts as changed; a config unreadable at HEAD or in the index refuses the commit; this config must protect itself. Globs use fnmatch: '*' also matches '/'. ff_private_retired names FF paths that exist only in history; they classify history and must match no tracked file (refused at commit time without override). Host files (Main.gd, World.gd, project.godot) are protected only in named parts: protected_definitions maps a path to {top-level GDScript definition: reason}, fingerprinted per definition by the FL-4781 gate's normalizer together with every top-level const it reads; protected_settings maps project.godot to {section/key glob: reason}, compared per key after normalization. A change to a protected part needs the trailer; other edits do not. A named definition or exact key that no longer exists is refused at commit time and fails --check, so a rename cannot drop protection silently. A host file must not name an FF-private res:// path in a string. Shader includes are found the way Godot's ShaderPreprocessor finds them (comments removed first); a GLSL include directive that RenderShaderSource.gd would not expand is refused. Owner: scripts/render_lane_boundary.py.
